run.procedureSummary: Charge: add each cycle's six charges to crucibles 1-6. Crucibles may go overfull here. Overflow: take crucibles 1 to 6 in turn. Any melt above a crucible's working volume moves into the next crucible, so a crucible that has just received melt can overflow in its own turn. Crucible 6's excess goes to slag. State check: this uses the quantities after overflow. A BASE crucible at or above its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. A SUPERHEATED crucible at or below its lower mark becomes BASE. Anything else keeps its state, and each change is logged. Tap: every draw is worked out from the post-overflow quantities before any melt moves. A BASE crucible draws floor(q/4), which goes to slag. A SUPERHEATED crucible draws floor(q/2), which goes up the return launder to crucible i-1, except that crucible 1's draw goes to slag. A crucible left overfull by return melt stays that way until the next cycle's overflow, and after cycle 5 it stays as it is. Emergency tap: checked once per cycle, after the tap. If the six crucibles total strictly more than 38, each one loses floor(q/2) to slag and keeps the rest, and the cycle is logged. States do not change here. Report after cycle 5.

openPoints.point: Rounding of the emergency halving: the write-up does not say whether the removed half or the kept half is rounded down
openPoints.assumption: The removed amount is floor(q/2) and the crucible keeps the rest, the same rule as 'splits round down' applied to the draw, as in the tap
BASE draw is floor(q/4) and SUPERHEATED draw is floor(q/2). The drawn amount is rounded down

openPoints.point: When the emergency check runs and where its threshold falls
openPoints.assumption: It runs once per cycle as the last step, after the tap, on the six-crucible total. It fires only above 38, so a total of exactly 38 (cycle 3) does not fire

openPoints.point: Which quantities the tap draws use
openPoints.assumption: Draws use the quantities after overflow (the state-check quantities), all worked out at once. Return melt that arrives does not change the draw of the crucible receiving it in the same cycle

openPoints.point: Whether crucible 6's overflow and crucible 1's return draw count as slag
openPoints.assumption: Both go to slag and are in the slag tally

openPoints.point: Whether the emergency tap affects states
openPoints.assumption: No. States change only at the state check

No overflow runs after the tap. Any overfull crucible waits for the next cycle's overflow step. In cycles 1, 4 and 5 the overfull crucible 2 was cut back by the emergency halving, and the final quantities are all within working volume
